claims.text: The driver did arrive inside the STANDARD 50 m arrival radius — the first qualifying in-geofence fix in his own trace coincides with the marked arrival at 12:48:56 (derived.arrival.dwell_start_offset_sec = 0.0) — so this case is not about whether he showed up. It turns on dwell, and under POL-NS-01 limb (c) the fee requires the driver to have held position inside the geofence for a continuous dwell of at least the free waiting period in force, which for this trip is trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180 seconds. The longest qualifying in-geofence run runs from 12:48:56 to 12:50:31: 95 continuous seconds, with 11 qualifying fixes. Limb (c) fails, and with it the charge.

POL-NS-06 makes a waiting-period shortfall a strict-liability refund: where the effective in-geofence dwell, computed under POL-NS-02 and corrected where necessary under POL-NS-05, is shorter than the free waiting period in force, the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages. The required minimum for this trip is 180 seconds; the measured dwell is 95 seconds; the shortfall is 85 seconds. The SGD 4.50 cancellation fee line on EV-FARE-03104 must therefore be refunded in full, and no driver compensation is payable on this route.

POL-NS-01 limb (d) independently fails. It requires the trip to have been terminated by the driver at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed. The dwell clock runs from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the arrival tap, so a 180 second dwell starting at 12:48:56 would not have elapsed until 12:51:56; the trip record shows the driver cancelled at 12:50:34, 82 seconds early. The platform's own wait timer agrees: it started at 12:48:58 and the cancellation came 96 seconds later. Either way the termination precedes the elapse of the period the fee is charged for.

The only route by which the driver could add time to this dwell is closed twice over. POL-NS-06 limb (i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where the driver left and re-entered the arrival radius without travelling more than 300 m from the pin, and the trace here contains exactly one in-geofence interval (derived.arrival.accumulated_dwell.run_count = 1, longest_run_sec = 95.0), so there is no second interval to add. Limb (i) also requires a present and populated traffic_advisory of an admissible type, and EV-ADVIS-03104-01 is MISSING: it carries no payload and weight 0.0, with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. I disclose that impairment — the artifact can carry no fact and its absence is citable only — and its absence means no advisory covers this pickup road and limb (i) is unavailable to the driver.

The driver's counterparty statement that 'Rider was not visible' is contradicted by the rider's own track. Twenty-four qualifying rider fixes, from 12:47:45 to 12:51:12, place the rider's device between 3.2 m and 9.4 m of the pickup pin (min 3.16 m, max 9.40 m, mean 6.28 m) — inside the 100 m STANDARD rider presence radius set by the policy for this zone class — and they corroborate the rider's 12:49:56 chat message 'im at the lobby, coming out'. POL-NS-06 refunds this fee whether or not the rider was present; on this record the rider was in fact at the pin for the whole of the waiting window, which removes any residual basis for the charge.

Nothing in this record is impaired under POL-NS-08, so the deciding facts rest on clean evidence at weight 1.0 and no discount or escalation is engaged. The arrival marker's timestamp (12:48:56) coincides exactly with the first qualifying in-geofence fix, so there is no clock skew under limb (a); the trace covers 100.0% of the window with no gaps and 59 fixes, so there is no trace defect under limb (b); the chat log carries 2 messages, matching trip_record.chat_message_count = 2, with sequence numbering intact, so there is no chat defect under limb (c); and the fare_breakdown cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.50 equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, so there is no fare defect under limb (d). The shortfall of 85 seconds is therefore established on unimpaired evidence.

Limb (a) and limb (b) of POL-NS-01 are therefore satisfied, and the driver passes the POL-NS-02 proximity test on admissible fixes. POL-NS-05 is not engaged, and no false-arrival referral should be recorded against the driver. The 'I'm Here' marker was tapped at 12:48:56, the identical timestamp of the trace's first qualifying in-geofence fix, so the clause's distance trigger - the driver more than 300 m from the pickup pin at the marker - cannot be satisfied on this record: the driver was inside the 50 m arrival radius and the run beginning at that fix is the trace's in-geofence dwell, not a pass-through at 15 km/h or more. The rider's exoneration route under POL-NS-04 is closed at limb (b), and it should not be treated as an unanswered-message case. ruling.explanation:
The SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-03104 is refunded in full to the rider. Both sides agree on the facts, and the record supports the refund.

What the driver got right. The arrival was real. His 'I'm Here' tap at 12:48:56 (EV-TRIP-03104) coincides exactly with the first GPS fix inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and EV-GPS-03104 shows him holding there — 11 consecutive qualifying in-geofence fixes. POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (b) are therefore satisfied, and the POL-NS-05 false-arrival test is not engaged: at the marker he was inside the radius, not more than 300 m away and not moving at 15 km/h or more. No false-arrival referral is entered. The termination was also correctly coded RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises, so no mis-coded-reason referral arises; and the ledger reconciles (EV-FARE-03104 total_charged SGD 4.50 = platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd SGD 4.50), so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect.

Why the charge nonetheless fails. The fee needs the driver to have held position inside the geofence for the free waiting period in force — 180 seconds, read from EV-TRIP-03104 platform_policy.free_wait_sec. Under POL-NS-01(c) that clock runs from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the arrival tap. Here the two coincide, so the clock starts at 12:48:56. EV-GPS-03104 shows one continuous in-geofence run from 12:48:56 to 12:50:31: 95 seconds, an 85 second shortfall against the 180 required. Limb (c) fails, and limb (d) fails with it: the driver cancelled at 12:50:34, before the 180 seconds would have run out at 12:51:56 (the platform's own wait timer, started 12:48:58, had run only 96 seconds). POL-NS-06 then applies as strict liability — a waiting-period shortfall means the fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded.

The one route to lengthening the dwell, POL-NS-06 limb (i), is closed twice over. The trace contains a single in-geofence interval (run_count = 1), so there is no second interval to add; and the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-03104-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 — it carries no payload and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it can carry no fact and limb (i) is unavailable.

Points that do not change the result. The rider's POL-NS-04 exoneration route is closed because the driver did reply ('ok' at 12:50:11, fifteen seconds after the rider's 12:49:56 message), well inside the 120 second window, so that clause does not apply; it makes no difference because POL-NS-06 already refunds. The driver's counterparty statement that the rider 'was not visible' is not borne out by EV-GPS-03104, whose 24 rider fixes place the rider's device between 3.2 m and 9.4 m of the pickup pin (well inside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius) and corroborate the rider's 'im at the lobby, coming out'; but POL-NS-06 refunds regardless of rider presence, so nothing turns on it.

Evidence quality. No artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08 limbs (a)–(d): the arrival timestamp matches the nearest GPS fix (no clock skew), the trace covers 100% of the window with no gaps and 59 fixes, the chat log's 2 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count = 2 with intact sequence numbering, and the fare line reconciles. The deciding facts therefore rest on unimpaired artifacts at weight 1.0 (EV-GPS-03104 and EV-TRIP-03104, independent of each other), so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and confidence is 0.95, above the 0.70 floor. No escalation ground under POL-NS-09 is present.

Amount. The refund is the cancellation-fee line only: SGD 4.50 (EV-FARE-03104). No driver compensation is payable, because POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full and POL-NS-07 is therefore not reached. The monetary effect (SGD 4.50) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so this ruling executes automatically.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides' evidence converges on the same arithmetic, and the outcome for the rider is a full refund of the SGD 4.50 cancellation-fee line.

DRIVER — your arrival was genuine, but the fee still cannot stand. The trip record carries your driver_arrived event at 2026-08-17T12:48:56 (EV-TRIP-03104), and your own GPS trace (EV-GPS-03104) puts you inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from that same second, holding 11 consecutive qualifying fixes at the 10 s cadence. So POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (b) are satisfied, and I reject any suggestion of a false 'I'm Here' tap: the marker timestamp coincides exactly with the first qualifying in-geofence fix (dwell_start_offset_sec = 0.0), so POL-NS-05's distance and speed triggers are not engaged and no false-arrival referral is recorded against you.

The charge fails on the waiting period. Under POL-NS-01(c) the free waiting period in force for this trip is trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180 seconds, and the dwell clock runs from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the arrival tap. Your trace shows one continuous in-geofence run of 95 seconds, from 12:48:56 to 12:50:31, against the 180 seconds required — a shortfall of 85 seconds — and you terminated at 12:50:34, before the period elapsed. POL-NS-06 makes that shortfall a strict-liability refund of the cancellation-fee line whether or not the rider was present or responsive, and it expressly allows no driver compensation on this route; POL-NS-07 pays a driver only where POL-NS-01 holds in full, which it does not. The accumulation route in POL-NS-06(i) cannot help either: the trace contains a single in-geofence interval (run_count = 1), so there is no second interval to sum, and the traffic_advisory it also requires, EV-ADVIS-03104-01, is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — an absence that can be cited but carries no fact.

RIDER — you are refunded the full SGD 4.50. That is the cancellation_fee line on EV-FARE-03104 and the total_charged figure (SGD 4.50, with base fare, platform fee, distance, time and waiting-time fee all at SGD 0.00), and it equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect. Your 24 qualifying fixes (12:47:45–12:51:12) place your device between 3.2 m and 9.4 m of the pickup pin, well inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, and they corroborate your 12:49:56 message 'im at the lobby, coming out'. I note the driver's counterparty statement that you were 'not visible' is contradicted by that track; the statement carries no weight_multiplier and enters neither the minimum nor the maximum of the confidence cap. Your exoneration under POL-NS-04 does not independently fire — the driver replied 'ok' 15 seconds after your message, inside the 120 s window — but that makes no difference, because POL-NS-06 refunds on the shortfall alone.

On integrity and escalation: no POL-NS-08 limb fires. There is no clock skew (the marker and the first in-geofence fix share the timestamp 12:48:56), no trace gap (max_gap_sec = 0.0, 59 fixes, 100% coverage, rider track present), no chat defect (2 messages matching trip_record.chat_message_count = 2, sequence intact), and no fare defect. The deciding facts — the 95 s dwell against the 180 s minimum — rest on EV-GPS-03104 and EV-TRIP-03104, both at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0, and no POL-NS-09 trigger (confidence, direct contradiction on arrival/dwell/presence, repeat-party disputes, anti-farming, sole impaired evidence) applies. No escalation, and no referral: POL-NS-05(ii), POL-RD-06(c) and POL-RD-09(4) each require facts this record does not carry, and the reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW is one POL-NS-01(d) recognises, so no mis-coded-reason item arises.

The monetary effect, SGD 4.50, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so this refund executes automatically; either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

It turns on dwell, and under POL-NS-01 limb (c) the fee requires the driver to have held position inside the geofence for a continuous dwell of at least the free waiting period in force, which for this trip is trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180 seconds. The longest qualifying in-geofence run runs from 12:48:56 to 12:50:31: 95 continuous seconds, with 11 qualifying fixes. Limb (c) fails, and with it the charge.

POL-NS-06 makes a waiting-period shortfall a strict-liability refund: where the effective in-geofence dwell, computed under POL-NS-02 and corrected where necessary under POL-NS-05, is shorter than the free waiting period in force, the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages. The required minimum for this trip is 180 seconds; the measured dwell is 95 seconds; the shortfall is 85 seconds. The SGD 4.50 cancellation fee line on EV-FARE-03104 must therefore be refunded in full, and no driver compensation is payable on this route.

POL-NS-01 limb (d) independently fails. It requires the trip to have been terminated by the driver at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed. The dwell clock runs from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the arrival tap, so a 180 second dwell starting at 12:48:56 would not have elapsed until 12:51:56; the trip record shows the driver cancelled at 12:50:34, 82 seconds early. The platform's own wait timer agrees: it started at 12:48:58 and the cancellation came 96 seconds later. Either way the termination precedes the elapse of the period the fee is charged for.

The only route by which the driver could add time to this dwell is closed twice over. POL-NS-06 limb (i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where the driver left and re-entered the arrival radius without travelling more than 300 m from the pin, and the trace here contains exactly one in-geofence interval (derived.arrival.accumulated_dwell.run_count = 1, longest_run_sec = 95.0), so there is no second interval to add. Limb (i) also requires a present and populated traffic_advisory of an admissible type, and EV-ADVIS-03104-01 is MISSING: it carries no payload and weight 0.0, with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. I disclose that impairment — the artifact can carry no fact and its absence is citable only — and its absence means no advisory covers this pickup road and limb (i) is unavailable to the driver.

The driver's counterparty statement that 'Rider was not visible' is contradicted by the rider's own track. Twenty-four qualifying rider fixes, from 12:47:45 to 12:51:12, place the rider's device between 3.2 m and 9.4 m of the pickup pin (min 3.16 m, max 9.40 m, mean 6.28 m) — inside the 100 m STANDARD rider presence radius set by the policy for this zone class — and they corroborate the rider's 12:49:56 chat message 'im at the lobby, coming out'. POL-NS-06 refunds this fee whether or not the rider was present; on this record the rider was in fact at the pin for the whole of the waiting window, which removes any residual basis for the charge.

Nothing in this record is impaired under POL-NS-08, so the deciding facts rest on clean evidence at weight 1.0 and no discount or escalation is engaged. The arrival marker's timestamp (12:48:56) coincides exactly with the first qualifying in-geofence fix, so there is no clock skew under limb (a); the trace covers 100.0% of the window with no gaps and 59 fixes, so there is no trace defect under limb (b); the chat log carries 2 messages, matching trip_record.chat_message_count = 2, with sequence numbering intact, so there is no chat defect under limb (c); and the fare_breakdown cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.50 equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, so there is no fare defect under limb (d). The shortfall of 85 seconds is therefore established on unimpaired evidence.

The driver's arrival is real, and it is the kind of arrival POL-NS-02 is written to authenticate. The trip record carries a driver_arrived event at 2026-08-17T12:48:56 (EV-TRIP-03104), and the GPS trace independently places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from that very second, holding there for 11 consecutive in-radius fixes at the trace's 10 second cadence. Limb (a) and limb (b) of POL-NS-01 are therefore satisfied, and the driver passes the POL-NS-02 proximity test on admissible fixes. This was not a speculative or fabricated 'I'm Here' tap: the driver's own trace shows him approaching from roughly 7 km away and entering the radius at the marker's timestamp.

POL-NS-05 is not engaged, and no false-arrival referral should be recorded against the driver. The 'I'm Here' marker was tapped at 12:48:56, the identical timestamp of the trace's first qualifying in-geofence fix, so the clause's distance trigger - the driver more than 300 m from the pickup pin at the marker - cannot be satisfied on this record: the driver was inside the 50 m arrival radius and the run beginning at that fix is the trace's in-geofence dwell, not a pass-through at 15 km/h or more. The driver's fault on this trip was leaving the kerb too early; it was not claiming to be somewhere he was not.

The rider's exoneration route under POL-NS-04 is closed at limb (b), and it should not be treated as an unanswered-message case. The rider sent 'im at the lobby, coming out' at 12:49:56 and the driver replied 'ok' at 12:50:11 - fifteen seconds later, far inside the 120 second window - on a chat log whose msg_id sequence numbering is intact and whose read receipts are present. Because the driver did reply within 120 seconds, POL-NS-04 does not apply regardless of the content of the reply, and the dispute falls to be decided on the driver's own position and dwell rather than on driver silence.

Nothing in the driver's paperwork is defective, and whatever remedy issues should be confined to a single line. The termination was recorded under RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three reason codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises, so no mis-coded-reason referral of the kind DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE would attract is available here; and the ledger reconciles to the platform's own figure - SGD 4.50 charged against platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of SGD 4.50, with base fare, platform fee and waiting-time fee each at 0.00 - so there is no POL-NS-08(d) integrity defect and the only sum in play is the cancellation-fee line.

I do not contest the dwell arithmetic, and I do not ask the Judge to hold the fee chargeable on it. On the correct measure the effective in-geofence dwell is 95 seconds against the free waiting period of 180 seconds in force for this STANDARD pickup, read from platform_policy.free_wait_sec (the 300 second STANDARD figure retained in fee_schedule applies only to records authored before policy version 2 and is not applicable to a record that carries platform_policy) - an 85 second shortfall - so limb (c) of POL-NS-01 is not met and limb (d) fails with it, and POL-NS-06 points to a refund of the cancellation-fee line. I ask only that the ruling reflect the driver's genuine arrival and genuine wait, enter no false-arrival referral against him, and go no further than the SGD 4.50 line the ledger carries.
